summary.one_liner: A Python library and CLI that automatically inserts spaces between CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) text and adjacent Latin letters, digits, and symbols.
summary.what_it_does: It provides space_text() to return a string with spaces inserted between CJK characters and ANS (alphabetical letters, digits, symbols), space_file() to process a file with a given encoding, and has_proper_spacing() to check whether text already follows that spacing. A pangu-py command-line tool accepts text as an argument, via -f for a file, via -c to check and report a correction (exit code 1 when spacing is off), or from stdin. The README also lists sibling implementations for pangu.js, pangu.go, pangu.java, and a pangu.space HTTP API. Examples show it spacing mixed text like "DevOps", "Google", "Vim", and "rm -rf /*" inside Chinese sentences.
use_cases: Adding spaces between Chinese text and English words in documents
Cleaning up mixed CJK and Latin text in files
Checking whether text already has proper CJK spacing
Normalizing spacing in user-generated content via a CLI pipe
Formatting Japanese or Korean text mixed with English terms
notable: Single-purpose spacing rules: inserts spaces only between CJK and ANS text
Offers a library API, a CLI with check mode, and stdin input
Same spacing logic is also published as pangu.js, pangu.go, pangu.java, and an HTTP API
Can be run without installing via uvx
caveats: The README describes the spacing as opinionated, so output may not match every style guide
README does not describe other limitations or supported Python versions
keywords: insert spaces between chinese and english
